findings.title: Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET
findings.body: This GET invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a new notification level for the logged-in user. The URL is predictable, has no unsubscribe token, and bypasses check_xhr; Rails' normal CSRF protection does not validate GET requests. An attacker can therefore send a logged-in victim through a cross-site navigation to silence notifications for an accessible topic. Make GET display a confirmation and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST.

findings.title: Persist the unsubscribe change during client-side navigation
findings.body: This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. If an already-loaded Discourse application navigates to the unsubscribe URL client-side, the initial HTML request to TopicsController#unsubscribe never happens. The page nevertheless tells the user notifications will stop, while their subscription remains unchanged. The client-side flow needs to perform the subscription change explicitly.

findings.title: Mark unsubscription as an explicit notification preference change
findings.body: Saving notification_level directly bypasses the bookkeeping in TopicUser.change, particularly setting notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For an existing topic-user row whose reason is NULL, an unsubscribe can set the level to Muted but leave it eligible for automatic tracking. TopicUser.update_last_read then changes it back to Tracking once the reading-time threshold is met, undoing the mute and re-enabling notifications. Use the normal notification-change helper so the explicit preference is preserved.

findings.title: Handle an absent TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil: for example, a forwarded notification for a public topic can be opened by another logged-in account that has never visited that topic. Access to the topic does not guarantee a topic-user row exists. Dereferencing tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of unsubscribing. Treat the missing row as the default notification level and create the preference through TopicUser.change.

findings.title: Keep the topic URL optional in the shared unsubscribe footer
findings.body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation now unconditionally requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder still accepts add_unsubscribe_link without supplying that value. A previously supported call such as MessageBuilder.new(address, body: "hello", add_unsubscribe_link: true).body now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument instead of building an email. Both text and HTML footer generation use this translation. Preserve the generic preferences-only footer and add the topic paragraph only when a topic unsubscribe URL is available.

findings.title: Do not promise that Regular disables all topic notifications
findings.body: The confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but the controller changes Watching or Tracking users to Regular rather than Muted. Regular still allows notifications and notification emails for mentions and replies to the user, so the confirmation promises more than the operation provides. Describe the notifications that remain enabled, or change the operation to match the promise.
